description: Quality scoring rubric for BABOK Quality Audit Agent — one entry per stage

quality_criteria.description: Every quantitative KPI has a numeric baseline value
Every quantitative KPI has a numeric target value
Every deadline is a specific calendar date (not Q1/soon/TBD)
Budget range has currency and numeric bounds
ROI targets include payback period, NPV and IRR

consistency_checks.description: Scope items are consistent with regulatory requirements listed
RACI accountability assignments match stakeholder influence levels

generation_batches.title: Scope & context
generation_batches.instruction: Define what this project actually covers and excludes, in terms specific to the stated industry and systems — not a generic scope boilerplate.

generation_batches.title: Systems & stakeholders
generation_batches.instruction: Use the scope from the core batch above. Name real systems and real stakeholder roles implied by that scope; the RACI must reference the same roles listed in the Stakeholder Register, not generic placeholders.

generation_batches.title: Success criteria & communication
generation_batches.instruction: KPIs must have real numeric baseline/target values grounded in the project context, not placeholder numbers. Communication plan should name the stakeholder groups already established above.

generation_batches.title: Constraints & regulatory
generation_batches.instruction: Regulatory requirements must be consistent with the scope items from the core batch (only flag regulations actually implicated by what's in scope).

generation_batches.title: Open questions & sign-off
generation_batches.instruction: Use the complete document above as context. Open questions should surface real gaps left by earlier batches, not generic filler questions.

stage2.name: Current State Analysis (AS-IS)
required_sections: AS-IS Process Map or BPMN description

quality_criteria.description: Baseline metrics are numeric (not qualitative descriptions)
Each bottleneck cites a measurable impact
Volume metrics include unit of measure and time period

consistency_checks.description: All pain points from Stage 1 context are addressed in pain points analysis
System inventory matches system landscape from Stage 1

generation_batches.title: Process & pain points
sections: AS-IS Process Map or BPMN description
generation_batches.instruction: Describe the actual current process implied by Stage 1's scope, not a generic process template. Every pain point should be traceable to something in scope.

generation_batches.title: Baseline metrics & bottlenecks
generation_batches.instruction: Use the process map above. Baseline metrics need real units/time periods, not vague qualitative descriptions. Each bottleneck must cite a measurable impact tied to a step in the process map.

generation_batches.title: Sign-off
generation_batches.instruction: Use the complete document above as context.

stage3.name: Problem Domain Analysis
required_sections: Root Cause Analysis (5 Whys or Ishikawa)

quality_criteria.description: Each problem statement is measurable (contains numeric or observable criterion)
Root cause analysis goes at least 3 levels deep (3 Whys minimum)
Prioritisation matrix uses two quantifiable dimensions (e.g. Impact × Likelihood)

consistency_checks.description: Every root cause traces to a pain point from Stage 1 or bottleneck from Stage 2
Compliance-related problems are ranked high priority (consistent with Stage 1 regulatory requirements)

generation_batches.title: Root causes & problem statements
sections: Root Cause Analysis (5 Whys or Ishikawa)
generation_batches.instruction: Trace every root cause to a specific pain point or bottleneck from Stage 1/2 — go at least 3 levels deep (3 Whys minimum), not a single surface-level cause. Problem statements must be measurable, not vague complaints.

generation_batches.title: Prioritisation & impact
generation_batches.instruction: Use the problem statements above. Prioritise using two quantifiable dimensions (e.g. Impact x Likelihood), and rank any compliance-related problem high priority if Stage 1 identified applicable regulations.

generation_batches.title: Sign-off
generation_batches.instruction: Use the complete document above as context.

quality_criteria.description: Every acceptance criterion is testable (produces observable, verifiable outcome)
NFRs contain numeric thresholds (e.g. response time < 2s, availability >= 99.5%)
Each FR has a unique ID (FR-NNN format)
MoSCoW prioritisation applied to all requirements

consistency_checks.description: Every FR traces to at least one problem from Stage 3 RTM
Regulatory compliance requirements present when Stage 1 identified applicable regulations
No requirement addresses a problem not identified in Stage 3 (scope creep check)

generation_batches.title: Core requirements
generation_batches.instruction: Produce these sections only. Every FR must trace to a problem from Stage 3 — do not invent requirements addressing problems not identified there. NFRs need real numeric thresholds (e.g. response time < 2s), not vague adjectives like 'fast' or 'secure'. Do not reference RTM/Change Control/Compliance yet.

generation_batches.title: Derived cross-references
generation_batches.instruction: Build on the FR/NFR already in the document above. Every FR-NNN must appear in the RTM with no gaps. Acceptance criteria must each produce an observable, testable outcome.

generation_batches.title: Compliance & sign-off
generation_batches.instruction: Use the complete document above as context. Only include regulatory requirements Stage 1 actually identified as applicable.

quality_criteria.description: Every major problem from Stage 3 has a corresponding design element addressing it
Projected improvements are quantified and tied to Stage 1 KPI targets
Each design decision documents alternatives considered and rationale for choice

consistency_checks.description: Every must-have FR from Stage 4 has a corresponding TO-BE design element
Integration points match systems identified in Stage 2 system inventory
No new scope items introduced without explicit change request reference

generation_batches.title: TO-BE process & key decisions
generation_batches.instruction: Every must-have FR from Stage 4 needs a corresponding TO-BE design element addressing it. Each design decision must document alternatives considered and why this one was chosen, not just a bare conclusion.

generation_batches.title: Architecture & UX impact
generation_batches.instruction: Use the TO-BE process and decisions above. Integration points must match systems from Stage 2's system inventory. Quantify projected improvements against the Stage 1 KPI targets, don't just describe them qualitatively.

generation_batches.title: Sign-off
generation_batches.instruction: Use the complete document above as context.

quality_criteria.description: Each milestone has a specific calendar date and measurable completion criterion
Each phase has estimated effort in person-days or person-months
Critical path explicitly identifies the longest dependency chain

consistency_checks.description: Every gap traces to at least one requirement from Stage 4
Total resource plan cost is within budget constraints from Stage 1
Roadmap end date is on or before target date from Stage 1

generation_batches.title: Gaps & phasing
generation_batches.instruction: Every gap must trace to a specific requirement from Stage 4 — not a generic AS-IS/TO-BE delta. Phase the work with real trade-off reasoning (why this phasing, not another), each phase with an effort estimate in person-days/months.

generation_batches.title: Resources & timeline
generation_batches.instruction: Use the phasing above. Resource plan total cost must fit within Stage 1's budget constraints. Milestones need specific calendar dates and a measurable completion criterion. Critical path must explicitly name the longest dependency chain, and the roadmap end date must not exceed Stage 1's target date.

generation_batches.title: Sign-off
generation_batches.instruction: Use the complete document above as context.

stage7.name: Risk Assessment & Mitigation
required_sections: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA, if GDPR applicable)

quality_criteria.description: Each risk has a numeric likelihood score and impact score (1–5 scale)
Each mitigation action is assigned to a named owner with a target date
Residual risk is quantified after mitigation (not just described)

consistency_checks.description: High-priority risks are consistent with compliance requirements from Stage 1
Technical risks reference integration points from Stage 5
DPIA section present when GDPR or equivalent was identified in Stage 1

generation_batches.title: Risk register & prioritisation
generation_batches.instruction: Every risk needs a numeric likelihood and impact score (1-5 scale), not a qualitative label alone. High-priority risks must be consistent with the compliance requirements identified in Stage 1 — don't under-rank a compliance risk.

generation_batches.title: Mitigation & residual risk
sections: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA, if GDPR applicable)
generation_batches.instruction: Use the risk register above. Every mitigation action needs a named owner and target date. Include the DPIA section if Stage 1 identified GDPR or an equivalent regulation. Quantify residual risk after mitigation, don't just describe it.

generation_batches.title: Sign-off
generation_batches.instruction: Use the complete document above as context.

quality_criteria.description: Every financial parameter cites a data source (vendor quote, survey, baseline data)
Sensitivity analysis varies at least 2 key assumptions (e.g. adoption rate, implementation cost)
NPV discount rate is explicitly stated and justified
Executive Recommendation clearly states go/no-go with rationale

consistency_checks.description: Implementation costs align with resource plan from Stage 6
Savings estimates trace to KPI improvements identified in Stage 1
Payback period is within the maximum acceptable period stated in Stage 1
Risks and uncertainties in financial model reference Stage 7 risk register

generation_batches.title: Costs & benefits
generation_batches.instruction: Implementation costs must align with the resource plan from Stage 6. Every financial parameter needs a cited data source (vendor quote, survey, baseline data) — no invented figures presented as fact.

generation_batches.title: Financial metrics
generation_batches.instruction: Use the cost-benefit figures above. State and justify the NPV discount rate explicitly. Savings estimates must trace to the KPI improvements identified in Stage 1, and the payback period must be within Stage 1's maximum acceptable period.

generation_batches.title: Sensitivity & recommendation
generation_batches.instruction: Vary at least 2 key assumptions (e.g. adoption rate, implementation cost) in the sensitivity analysis, referencing risks/uncertainties from the Stage 7 risk register. The Executive Recommendation must clearly state go/no-go with rationale, not a hedge.

generation_batches.title: Sign-off
generation_batches.instruction: Use the complete document above as context.
